<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 07559ce5ae8b9636b36e6a591bb584e3309fd1ad`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 07559ce5ae8b9636b36e6a591bb584e3309fd1ad` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4f05f673c747fbc7d34485f8c367a45b2ff94dea` — the merge of head `8f2196e8511133537713257bc942777ca591be1d` into base `07559ce5ae8b9636b36e6a591bb584e3309fd1ad`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4f05f673c747fbc7d34485f8c367a45b2ff94dea && git checkout 4f05f673c747fbc7d34485f8c367a45b2ff94dea
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 07559ce5ae8b9636b36e6a591bb584e3309fd1ad 8f2196e8511133537713257bc942777ca591be1d && git checkout -B drift-repro 07559ce5ae8b9636b36e6a591bb584e3309fd1ad && git merge --no-ff 8f2196e8511133537713257bc942777ca591be1d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 07559ce5ae8b9636b36e6a591bb584e3309fd1ad
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 07559ce5ae8b9636b36e6a591bb584e3309fd1ad` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `2f7e23d754c18fe1da5e7d2ea9f7aa9ab83f51c8`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs read: card #31264 (body, claim 6712858125, os-dev-report 6713325766: 2 comments, all of them), PR #31276 (body, 7-file list, net diff against merge-base `455229e7`), and the head's check-runs. The diff's cited code was read at `pr31276` with `git show` / `git grep` only.

- **`os validate --target`, `allowCode: false` (`restriction-profile.ts`): widening, RIGHT.** `CODE_KEYS` now leaves out `NEVER_REACHES_TARGET = {'devPlugins'}`, so a stack that was refused before for `devPlugins[i]` is now accepted. `plugins` beside it is still refused: the unit case pins exactly one `plugins[0]` row, and the door test keeps its exact `allowCode: false` rows with `devPlugins` in the fixture. Removing the `dev plugin '…'` label branch retires an output string that no doc or skill names (`git grep "dev plugin '"` finds no hits). `os validate` judges the loaded config, not an artifact, so "never reaches a target" holds for any artifact this CLI builds. `UNMANAGED_INSTALL_KEY_DISPOSITIONS` is unchanged, as the card required.
- **The published artifact loses `devPlugins` (`compile.ts:1181`, at the one artifact write, after `demoStaff`): no narrowing for any reader I could reach.** Reader by reader:
  - *The CLI's own loaders.* `stackBootPlugins(config, flags.dev)` (`serve.ts:3302`, `stack-collections.ts:177`) reads the loaded config, and only under the `--dev` flag. The artifact-fallback boot starts from `config = {}`. `createStandaloneStack` returns only named keys from the artifact (`plugins` it builds itself, plus `requires`, `objects`, `manifest`, `permissions`, `positions`, `i18n`), never `devPlugins`. `format.ts` stats come from the config. `one-shot-settings.ts` and `verify/harness.ts` read `plugins` only. Not a narrowing.
  - *Runtime `loadArtifactBundle`.* No reader of the key exists. The new build test pins the key absent from what it returns. Not a narrowing.
  - *Stack schema on an artifact.* `devPlugins` is `.optional()` (`stack.zod.ts:1407`), so its absence parses. An artifact built before this change, which still carries the key, still parses and installs. Not a narrowing.
  - *`os package publish` / `os deploy`.* publish snapshots the file as it is, with no check on this key. deploy spawns `compile --output dist/objectstack.json` (`deploy-build.ts:22`), so this change covers it. Versions already published keep the key in `manifest_json`. Not a narrowing.
  - *Migration chain relevance walk* (`spec/migrations/chain.ts:118`). A listed `devPlugins` reads `unknown`. For a fresh artifact the key is gone, so the walk can now read `absent`, which moves a semantic TODO into the `--all` list. That refuses nothing, and it is accurate, since no target boot loads the key. Not a narrowing.
  - *Unmanaged install* (`metadata-protocol/package-unmanaged-install.ts:407-419`, also used through `cloud-connection` local marketplace installs). The disposition table is unchanged, but a newly built artifact no longer carries the key. So `os package install ./dist/objectstack.json --install-mode unmanaged` no longer refuses a stack just for declaring `devPlugins`. This is a **second widening**. It is RIGHT (the list is never loaded on a target) and falls inside the declared `(widening)` arm. It is **not named** in the changeset or PR body, and the PR's line "an unmanaged install still refuses `devPlugins` as code" is true of the table but not of the end-to-end door for a rebuilt artifact. See should-fix 1.
  - *hotcrm docs prose* (`sandbox-and-releases{,.zh-Hans,.zh-Hant}.mdx:127`). It lists the 42 keys `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` accepts. The schema still accepts `devPlugins`, so the sentence stays true. It is prose, not a reader, and the drift already there (no `demoStaff`) predates this PR. Not a narrowing.
  - *objectstack-ai/cloud: NOT MEASURED* (403 / no access, declared in the PR body and the report). I judge this a **declared residual, not a blocker**, for three reasons. The published schema describes the key as "Plugins to load only in development (CLI dev command)", so a target-side loader would be reading against the spec. Every version already published keeps the key. The change reverts in one line. It does leave the card's Owed item 1 condition ("confirm nothing in the cloud control plane reads the key first") and the claim's serial stop ("a cloud reader … stops the work after item 1") **unevaluated**. See should-fix 2.
- **Docs: RIGHT.** The quick-start sentence that listed what `os build` drops now names both keys. The `os compile` section of `deployment/cli.mdx` lists no dropped keys, so leaving it unchanged is correct.
- **Pins: adequate.** The build test checks the key is absent by key, by text, and from `loadArtifactBundle`, with `objects` surviving as the control and the `demoStaff` case on the same build. The reader case and the door case are described above. The dev's ablation legs (2 failed / 29 passed; 1 failed / 1 passed) are declared and I did not re-run them.
- **Build summary.** Its `Runtime:` row still counts `devPlugins` from the config. That is declared in the PR's acceptance notes and refuses nothing.
- **Check-runs on the head:** 49 read. 32 success, 12 skipped, 0 failed, 5 in progress: `Test Core (1/8)` through `(5/8)`. Those five must read green before ACCEPT. The PR is also still a **draft** (`mergeable: true`, `mergeable_state: blocked`).

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/31264-build-drops-dev-plugins.md` gives `'@objectstack/cli': patch`. Both changed source files ship in the cli `dist/`, so `skip-changeset` would have been wrong and was rightly not used. `Metadata-protocol: none` is RIGHT: an author can still write `devPlugins`, and the spec is untouched. Under AGENTS.md a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`, so the level matches.

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` starts a line in both the PR body and the changeset, and it is RIGHT. Two accept-sets widen (`os validate --target`, and in effect unmanaged install of a rebuilt artifact). No published reader narrows (the reader list in ① above). There is no `!` in the title, so no dogfood battery is owed. This also settles the claim's "seat amends to `yes (narrowing)` if it does" clause: no amendment. `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` are green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`:** `[]`. Nothing to answer.
- **Cloud unreachable** (summary, PR "Cross-repo check"): a declared residual, as judged in ①. **Escalated:** #31264 stays open through `Part of`. A seat with objectstack-ai/cloud access should check whether anything reads `manifest_json.devPlugins`, or enforces a restriction profile server-side, before the spec docblock states "never reaches a target".
- **Spec docblock, left to the spec seat:** the brief leaves this to the spec seat on purpose. **Escalated to the spec seat as the card's open half.** Until it lands, the published `allowCode` docblock (`restriction-profile.zod.ts`, "`false` refuses every one of them … code plugins") and the CLI reader diverge on `devPlugins`. The exact sentence is in the PR body.
- **Serial constraint #31239** (the claim says to read its claim and open PR before editing `restriction-profile.ts`): the report does not say this was done, and #31239 is outside my inputs. The PR is textually mergeable against `main` now. **Escalated to the seat:** whichever of the two PRs lands second reconciles `restriction-profile.ts`.
- **Deviations:**
  - *`pr_create` without labels:* moot, since the auto-labeler applied `documentation`, `size/m`, `tests` and `tooling`.
  - *No assignees, and `os-dev.md` rule 2 conflicts with AGENTS.md:* a process-text conflict, not a contract issue. **Escalated to the PM.**
  - *Unit-tier timeout:* re-run to a lock VERDICT (401/401). Accepted.
  - *`check:skill-examples` / `check:i18n-coverage` exit 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET):* re-run green after building the closures. CI's families answer for the head in any case. Accepted.
- **`security_findings`:** none. **`out_of_scope_findings`:** none.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-gi4qb9`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5p3T5YWhLjurajudnQ`

**VERDICT: PASS**

- should-fix 1: Name the second widening in the changeset body and the PR's Clause-② line. A newly built artifact no longer carries `devPlugins`, so `os package install … --install-mode unmanaged` (and the cloud-connection local installs) no longer refuse a stack that declares it. Reword "an unmanaged install still refuses `devPlugins` as code" so it applies to a bundle that carries the key (an old artifact), not to a fresh build.
- should-fix 2: Carry the unmeasured objectstack-ai/cloud reader (`manifest_json.devPlugins`, and any server-side restriction-profile enforcement) on #31264 as an explicit residual for a seat with cloud access, ahead of the spec docblock sentence.
- Before ACCEPT: `Test Core (1/8)` through `(5/8)` must read green, and the PR must leave draft.
